subdomain: 3.1 Evaluate tool/agent configuration for capability bloat

en.question: A telemetry assistant has four compact, necessary tools and selects them correctly. Its sensor query returns thousands of readings, although the task needs a per-device aggregate and every out-of-range reading. Most context tokens come from these results rather than tool definitions. Which change addresses the measured bloat without losing required evidence?

options.text: Aggregate readings in the tool layer and return the requested summary plus all out-of-range records.
options.note: Filtering and aggregation before model ingestion target the large intermediate results. Preserving every exception maintains the evidence required by this task.

options.text: Introduce tool search and defer all four existing tool definitions.
options.note: Deferring compact definitions addresses initial catalog context, not the thousands of returned readings. It adds discovery without materially reducing this bottleneck.

options.text: Shorten the four tool descriptions and remove optional-argument examples to reduce the token load.
options.note: This reduces definition tokens rather than the large returned dataset. The measurements show that compact definitions are not the dominant source of context use.

options.text: Return only the first page of readings and let the model infer device-level totals.
options.note: An arbitrary page omits readings and may hide exceptions. Aggregates inferred from an incomplete sample do not satisfy the requirement for complete device summaries.

references.title: Anthropic Engineering: Introducing advanced tool use
